title: content-v1: accept a directory whose on-disk case differs from Git's listing; refuse only distinct tracked paths that are one file on disk
outcome: content-v1 no longer forces on-disk path case to match Git's listing; it refuses only a real collision of distinct tracked paths on one file.
acceptance: On Windows with core.ignoreCase=true, a worktree where Git lists files under one directory in two case spellings (as Phoenix's F# CompilerOptions/Fsc and /fsc) gets a content-v1 revision instead of a refusal, by a test in the repository.

Two distinct tracked paths that differ only by case and/or NFC/NFD normalization and resolve to one file on disk are refused with an error naming both paths, by a test. Hard links whose names are not equal under the simple Unicode fold plus NFC/NFD are not newly refused; terminal symlinks are treated exactly as today.
A parent directory that is a link or junction leading elsewhere is still refused, by the existing or a new test.
The content-v1 value for a worktree without case-spelling differences is byte-identical before and after the change, by a test pinning a known value.

completion.summary: Landed content-v1 spelling admission in 0bfbb90d; Windows FULL 5/5 green, focused 54/54; all revised criteria linked to observed evidence.
